id: Pachyman + The Lahaar-San Fran, Wellington -Ticket Master
name: Pachyman + The Lahaar
long_description:
A recent review by 13thfloor.co.nz of a Pachyman set at Whammy celebrated the way Pachy used his magic sound to "immediately create a space nobody wanted to leave". We didn't want him to leave either, so we're bringing him back to Aotearoa this January. On Sunday 24 January he takes over Pōneke's hallowed San Fran for a double header with Trans-Tasman supergroup The Lahaar.

Over four albums, Pachyman has proven himself a dedicated craftsman in the lineage of dub reggae. He has mastered the methods of King Tubby and Scientist: vintage gear, glorious walls of sound, and an intuitive grasp of the power of repetition. Since his triumphant last visit in early 2025, Pachy "Pachyman" Garcia has released what critics are calling his most adventurous record yet, the dubtastic Another Place. On it he brings together the many scenes that have recontextualised dub, from the synth-pop of William Onyeabor and Yellow Magic Orchestra to Basic Channel's amniotic dub techno. With even stronger Latin flavours running through his sublime Lovers Rock and Studio One-inspired sounds, this will be a supercharged version of the Pachyman shows we've seen before.

Standing toe to toe with him are The Lahaar. The band brings together some of the brightest lights of the Australian and New Zealand jazz and electronic soul scenes: Julien Dyne, Horatio Luna and Lachlan Stuckey (Surprise Chef), and a revolving cast featuring members of Fat Freddy's Drop, The Circling Sun and Avantdale Bowling Club. Their self-titled debut on the UK's Soundway Records draws on late-'70s New York proto-rap disco instrumentals, Nigerian boogie, Jamaican dub and vintage cop-movie funk. Live, they're a full-blown big band of horns, flutes, vibraphone and congas, moving from high-energy percussive dance-floor heat into deep, meditative dub. It's the perfect match for Pachy's dubwise science.

Two headline acts and one very big night. Don't sleep on it.

"Pachyman is not to be slept on" – Aquarium Drunkard




San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

id: Slow Pilot (Belgium) - Performing the songs of Jeff Buckley-San Fran, Wellington -Ticket Master
name: Slow Pilot (Belgium) - Performing the songs of Jeff Buckley
long_description:
Singer Pieter Peirsman delivers a breathtaking vocal performance, capturing Buckley’s tone and emotional intensity. Grace (Lover You Should’ve Come Over, Hallelujah, Last Goodbye) is performed in full. Plus a special encore including Everybody Here Wants You

Direct from Belgium, Slow Pilot invite audiences into the world of Jeff Buckley, performing his music with sensitivity, precision and a deep respect honouring the songs that still mean so much to so many

Slow Pilot are the only band worldwide capable of awakening the true soul, mystery, and magic of Jeff Buckley’s work. Singer Pieter Peirsman delivers a breathtaking vocal performance, capturing Buckley’s tone and emotional intensity with incredible accuracy. The classic album Grace (Lover You Should’ve Come Over, Hallelujah, Last Goodbye, Forget Her) is performed in its entirety, honoring the album’s raw beauty, emotional intensity, and timeless songwriting. As a bonus there will be a selection of additional songs from the Jeff Buckley songbook (Everybody Here Wants You, I Know It’s Over)

Jeff Buckley remains one of the most captivating and influential figures in modern music history. His singular studio album Grace has long transcended cult status, becoming a global touchstone for artists and audiences across generations and borders. Today, Buckley’s legacy continues to grow and resonate internationally, inspiring new listeners while remaining deeply meaningful to those who have carried his music with them for years.

That renewed global attention has been further intensified by the recent release of the acclaimed documentary It’s Never Over, Jeff Buckley, which has reignited worldwide fascination with his life, his voice, and his artistic depth. The ongoing attention around Buckley once again highlights what fans have always known. His music remains emotionally powerful, fragile, and strikingly relevant.

For the many fans who never had the chance to experience Jeff Buckley live, this is an excellent second chance. For others, it is an opportunity to lose themselves completely in the extraordinary musical legacy Jeff Buckley left behind.

id: The Relatives Present : The Killers Hot Fuss +-San Fran, Wellington -Ticket Master
name: The Relatives Present : The Killers Hot Fuss +
long_description:
THE RELATIVES PRESENT: THE KILLERS — HOT FUSS +

One album. Every song. One unforgettable night.

2004 gave us Hot Fuss — the album that turned The Killers into one of the biggest bands in the world.

Now, The Relatives bring their version of this iconic record to the stage, live and loud, at San Fran.

From the opening bassline of Jenny Was a Friend of Mine to the undeniable rush of Mr. Brightside, Somebody Told Me, Smile Like You Mean It and All These Things That I’ve Done — this is your chance to experience Hot Fuss from start to finish, exactly as an album this legendary deserves: together, in a packed room, with the volume up.

And when Hot Fuss reaches its final note, the night isn’t over.

The Relatives will keep the party going with a special, hand-picked selection of crowd-pleasing hits and singalong favourites — spanning The Killers and other artists you know and love.
 So expect big choruses, familiar riffs, hands in the air and plenty of reasons to stay on the dance floor.

The Relatives are renowned for their energetic, polished live performances at major festivals, large-scale events, and packed venues across New Zealand. They bring the experience, energy and musicianship needed to do justice to one of the defining and most iconic albums of the 2000s - Hot Fuss — and then keep the party going long after the final track.

This isn’t just another night out.
 It’s HOT FUSS + — LIVE.

Bring your mates. Bring your best 2000s indie-rock energy. And prepare to sing every word.

If you know Hot Fuss, The Killers, or The Relatives, you already know why you need to be there.

--THE RELATIVES PRESENT: THE KILLERS — HOT FUSS +
 --San Fran
